title: SAS Returns to India After 17 Years With Mumbai-Copenhagen Flights
excerpt: Scandinavian Airlines will fly Copenhagen to Mumbai five times weekly starting October 1, offering NRIs a new one-stop connection to major US cities through its SkyTeam hub.
body:
• SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) is launching Copenhagen-Mumbai service five times weekly with an Airbus A330-300, marking its first India route in 17 years.
  • The flight offers one-stop connections from Mumbai to 10 major US cities including New York, Boston, Washington DC, Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.
  • SAS will operate 32 lie-flat business class seats, 56 premium economy seats, and 178 economy seats on the route, which launches October 1, 2026.
  • The service is the first-ever nonstop connection between Copenhagen and Mumbai, complementing Air India’s existing Delhi-Copenhagen route.

Scandinavian Airlines is returning to India after a 17-year absence, launching a five-times-weekly service between Copenhagen and Mumbai starting October 1, 2026. It will be the first nonstop flight ever operated between the two cities.

SAS, the flag carrier of Denmark, Sweden, and Norway, last served India in 2009 when it discontinued its Delhi route. The return signals renewed European carrier interest in India’s booming aviation market, which has grown substantially since the airline’s departure.

The Route and What It Offers

The airline will deploy its Airbus A330-300 on the route, configured with 32 lie-flat business class seats in a 1-2-1 layout, 56 premium economy seats (2-3-2), and 178 economy seats (2-4-2). The business class product features direct aisle access for every passenger, a competitive offering on the India-Europe segment.

"India is a key global market. The launch of our Copenhagen-Mumbai route reflects the growing demand for travel between Scandinavia and India."

— Anko van der Werff, CEO, SAS

The timing is strategic. Copenhagen serves as SAS’s primary hub and a SkyTeam alliance gateway, offering connections timed for smooth transfers to US-bound flights. Passengers from Mumbai can connect onward to New York (JFK), Newark, Boston, Washington DC, Atlanta, Chicago, Seattle, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Miami on a seasonal basis.

A New US-India Corridor for NRIs

For the Indian diaspora in the United States, the route opens a practical new one-stop option for US-India travel. Copenhagen’s compact airport and SAS’s coordinated SkyTeam scheduling mean connection times can be shorter than routing through the Gulf hubs that currently dominate US-India traffic.

The service complements rather than competes with Air India’s existing Delhi-Copenhagen nonstop, which serves northern India. With SAS covering Mumbai, the two airlines together provide Scandinavian connectivity to both of India’s largest gateway cities.

India’s Aviation Market Draws European Carriers Back

SAS’s return fits a broader pattern. European carriers have been expanding India service as the country’s air travel market grows at double-digit rates. Lufthansa, Air France-KLM, and British Airways have all added frequencies or new Indian cities in recent years, competing with Gulf carriers Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Etihad for the lucrative India-Europe and India-US connecting traffic.

India’s domestic air passenger traffic crossed 160 million in FY26, and outbound international travel is growing even faster as disposable incomes rise and visa regimes ease. For airlines like SAS that had stepped back during leaner years, the math has changed.

"This is the first-ever nonstop between Copenhagen and Mumbai. It fills a gap that business travelers and the diaspora community have felt for years."

— Aviation analysts, per Business Traveller

What to Know Before Booking

The five-weekly frequency means not every day will have service, so travelers should check schedules for their preferred travel dates. As a SkyTeam member, SAS flights are bookable through partner airline programs including Delta SkyMiles, and elite status benefits transfer across the alliance.

Fares and booking availability have not been officially announced, but the route is expected to open for reservations shortly. For NRIs planning winter travel to India, the October 1 launch date aligns well with the Diwali and holiday season travel surge.
